response.sql:
WITH major_counts AS (
    SELECT
        ma.major_id,
        ma.department,
        COUNT(me.member_id) AS member_count
    FROM member AS me
    JOIN major AS ma ON me.link_to_major = ma.major_id
    GROUP BY ma.major_id, ma.department
),
shares AS (
    SELECT
        major_id,
        department,
        member_count,
        1.0 * member_count / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM major_counts
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        major_id,
        department,
        member_count,
        share,
        share - AVG(share) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS above_department_avg
    FROM shares
)
SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, above_department_avg
FROM ranked
WHERE above_department_avg > 0
ORDER BY above_department_avg DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The department average is the unweighted arithmetic mean of the member shares for majors represented by at least one matched member; majors with zero matched members do not appear in the grouped counts.
